rules.name: LargeBarTightPauseNearHigh
rules.quote: 3-5 subsequent bars are small (< .5 the size of the large bullish bar) and are contained entirely within the range that extends .4*range_of_large_bar above and below the high of the large bar. Enter long
rules.description: A large bull bar (ON-12-a) N bars ago, and each of the N bars since is smaller than half its range and lies entirely within +/- 0.4 x its range of its high: long on the Nth such bar. Short mirrors around a large bear bar's low.

complexity.reason: Fixed-offset loop over pauseBars bars against one lagged bar.

library_check.evidence: MultiSessionPauseBreakout: a strong leg, a shallow pause inside it, entry on the close beyond the leg extreme. ON-12-b enters on the pause itself (no breakout), from a single large bar, with a size cap on each pause bar and a band centred on the big bar's high (so pause bars may trade above it).

notes: '3-5 subsequent bars' is the pauseBars range; it fires exactly pauseBars bars after the big bar.
Range ideas for the grid: pauseBars 3..5, bandFraction 0.3..0.5.

rules.name: LargeBarHoldThenCloseThroughMidpoint
rules.quote: Price holds between the 50% retracement level and 50% extension level for at least 5 bars. Enter short on the first candle to close below the 50% retracement level.
rules.description: Long side (mirror of the note's short): a large bear bar (ON-12-a, short shape) k bars ago; every close since stayed between its 50% extension below the low and its midpoint, for at least minHoldBars bars; this bar is the first to close above the midpoint: long. The note's trade: a large bull bar holds between midpoint and 50% extension above, short on the first close below the midpoint.

complexity.reason: Bounded backward scan for the anchor bar and a loop over closes since.

library_check.evidence: DeepPullbackRetracementFilter measures how far the close has retraced a window leg; nothing anchors on one large bar's midpoint and requires a hold band of closes for a minimum time before the first close through it.

notes: 'Price holds between' concretized on CLOSES (the trigger is a close); holding on whole-bar highs and lows is the alternative.
The midpoint (50% retracement) is the bar's midpoint for either colour; the 50% extension lies beyond the bar's close-side extreme.
No upper size cap in this note; maxRangeAtr 100 disables it.
maxBars bounds the scan (none in the note).

rules.name: LargeBarAtExtremeNextBarExtendsWeakClose
rules.quote: Large (>1.5 ATR) standard ... bearish bar that closes at or near the 20 bar low. Next bar makes a lower low but closes in the bottom 20% of the large standard bar's range. Enter short.
rules.description: Long side (mirror of the note): the prior bar is a large standard bull bar (ON-12-a at lag 1: range over 1.5 ATR, open in its bottom third, close in its top third) closing at or near the 20-bar high; this bar makes a higher high and closes in the top 20% of that bar's range (or above it): long.

complexity.reason: Fixed-lag bar arithmetic plus one Highest window.

library_check.evidence: ClimaxBar tests one large trend bar at lag 0 with a body fraction. ON-21 reads the large bar at lag 1, places its close near the window extreme, and needs a follow-through bar that extends AND closes strong. BreakoutBarLargeBodyLargeRange (Brooks) is a lag-0 size and body test only.

notes: The note's 'open and high near opposite extremes' is read as open and CLOSE (a 'standard' trend bar), about 1/3 each.
'At or near the 20 bar low' concretized as within nearAtr ATRs of the 20-bar low (window ending at the large bar, inclusive).
Kept as one pane-1 rule: the near-extreme test and the follow-through bar are both anchored on the lag-1 bar, so they cannot be split into independent placements.

rules.name: HugeBarOppositeInsideBarThenResume
rules.quote: Huge bearish bar with open near the high and close near the low that takes out X bar low ... Before the high of that bar gets taken out there is a bullish inside bar with open near low and close near the high. ... Enter short on the close of the first red candle.
rules.description: Long side (mirror): a huge bull bar b bars ago (ON-12-a shape, range at least K x ATR) whose high took out the prior X-bar high; later a bearish inside bar (open near its high, close near its low); since then nothing has traded below the huge bar's low; this bar is the first green bar after the inside bar: long. The note's trade is the short.
rules.book_order_type: enter on the first red candle's close; mechanized as next open

complexity.reason: Bounded backward scan with a lagged pattern anchor, an inside-bar search and an invalidation level.

library_check.evidence: InsideBar is the strict single-bar inside test. No rule chains a large breakout bar, a counter-coloured inside bar and a first resumption bar while the large bar's far extreme holds.

notes: 'Huge' has no number: hugeAtr default 2 ATR (the note's other 'large' bars are 1.5-2 ATR).
X (the taken-out window) is 10-50 in the note's two examples; default 20.
'Inside bar' read as inside its immediately preceding bar (strict, the InsideBar convention); inside the huge bar itself is the alternative.
Note: the invalidation is the huge bar's OPEN-side extreme being taken out (the short's 'high of the bearish bar').

rules.name: LargeBarInsideRunCloseBeyond
rules.quote: Bar 1 is a large (>1 ATR) bearish bar with body > .5x the range. Bars 2-X are contained entirely within the range of bar 1. Bar X+1 does not break the high of bar 1 but does close below it.
rules.description: Long side (mirror): bar 1, X bars ago, is a large bull bar (range over K x ATR, body over half its range); bars 2..X lie entirely within bar 1's range; this bar (X+1) does not trade below bar 1's low but closes above bar 1's high: long. The note's .3 is the short; .4 trades the same bear pattern long (reverse placement).

complexity.reason: Fixed-offset loop against one lagged bar.

library_check.evidence: ConsecutiveInsideBars chains inside relations bar-to-previous-bar; ON-40-a needs every bar contained in the FIRST bar (a mother-bar box), a large trend-bodied mother bar, and a close beyond the mother bar's far side. The mother-bar test alone is ClimaxBar(1, N, 0.5) (Brooks) at a lag.

notes: 'Closes below it' read as below bar 1's LOW (TRIAGE; the drawing shows the entry there).
Containment inclusive (high <= high1, low >= low1); 'does not break the high' read as high <= high1 (short case).
Exactly containedBars inside bars; range 1-4. 'At least' would be a scan.
ATR length unstated; 20 assumed, read at bar 1.

rules.name: NewWindowLowAboveLongerLow
rules.quote: Signal candle is a large bar (>= 2 ATR14) with a low below the X bar low but above the Y*X (Y ~ 2) low.
rules.description: This bar's low is below the lowest low of the prior X bars but above the lowest low of the prior Y x X bars: a new short-window low that is not a new long-window low. Long. Short mirrors at highs. 20250208.1b is this rule alone; .1 adds ON-29-b and ON-29-c.
rules.pseudocode:
longN = (int)(longFactor * lookback);
return low[0] < lowest(low, lookback)[1] && low[0] > lowest(low, longN)[1];

library_check.origin: Davey EEC (HighestHighBreakout, added with the EEC batch 0b6dea8)
library_check.evidence: HighestHighBreakout's short side is low at or below the N-bar lowest low (window including the current bar); placed flipped it is the 'new X-bar low' half. ON-29-a is strict against the window ending one bar ago and adds the outer bound (not a Y x X low), which no rule has. BullReversalBarAtNewLow and FailedBreakoutBeyondExtreme (Brooks) read the same new-low term with other second halves.

notes: X 25-50 (default 25), Y 2-3 (default 2) from the note. Y x X is truncated to an integer bar count.
Split per 'parameterize, don't author twice': .1b = ON-29-a alone, .1 = ON-29-a + ON-29-b + ON-29-c.

rules.name: BearBarTopHalfUntouchedLong
rules.quote: Strong bearish bar (>1 ATR, body significant fraction of candle) No prices in top half of bar for last ~10-15 bars. Enter long counter trend
rules.description: The bar W bars ago is a strong bear bar (range >= K x ATR, body >= F of range, close < open), and none of the W bars after it traded into its top half (every high below its midpoint). On the bar the window completes: long (counter-trend). Short mirrors on a strong bull bar whose bottom half stays untouched.
rules.sides: mirrored (as written the long fades a bear bar; the short fades a bull bar)

complexity.reason: lagged bar test with an ATR as of that bar

library_check.evidence: ClimaxBar is the strong-bar half at lag 0; nothing waits W bars for the bar's top half to stay untraded. Delayed by construction (Decision 9).

notes: atrAt(W) is the ATR as of the bear bar; reading the current ATR instead would be simpler (a choice to confirm in authoring).
Pseudocode is the as-written long side; here the long condition is the one that reads a BEAR bar.

rules.name: TargetAtSignalBarOpen
rules.quote: Enter long counter trend with target of bearish bars open
rules.description: Long profit target at the open of the bar W+1 bars before the fill bar (P14's bear bar), frozen at entry: exit when the high reaches it. Short mirrors at the bull bar's open.
rules.pseudocode:
if (ctx.BarsSinceEntry() == 0) target = open[W + 1];   // read every bar, freeze conditionally
exitLong = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && el_ge(high[0], target);

complexity.reason: captures a level on the fill bar

library_check.evidence: EntryBarExtremeTarget captures the signal bar's far extreme on the fill bar ([1]); this captures the open of a bar W+1 back. Coupled to P14's W, so the pair must share the value.

notes: A long needs the open above the entry for this to be a target; it is by construction (the bear bar opened near its high, above its untouched midpoint).

rules.name: BreakawayPullbackBreak
rules.quote: Big breakaway move (multiple bars OR ATR cutoff). Measured from open of first breakaway bar to high of the move. Pullback consisting of multiple bars (3-5) which do not break the high of the move but only pullback a small fraction (top 20-30%). Enter long on break above the high.
rules.description: Move = the run of consecutive up-close bars ending at the bar t that holds the highest high of the last (maxRun + maxPullback) bars; height = H - open[first bar of the run]. Breakaway if the run is at least minRunBars long OR height >= A x ATR. Pullback = bars t-1..1, between minPullback and maxPullback of them, all with high < H and low >= H - f x height. Long on the close above H. Short mirrors.
rules.book_order_type: buy stop above the move high; mechanized as a close above it

complexity.reason: variable-length move recognition plus a bounded pullback

library_check.evidence: BreakoutPullbackEntry (breakout bar, 1-10 bar pullback, close above the pullback high) and FirstPullbackAfterSpike (strong-bar spike, first pullback) are the Brooks relatives; neither bounds the pullback to the top fraction of the move or breaks the move's own high.

notes: The move definition (consecutive up-close run) is a concretization; see open_questions.

rules.name: ExtremePairRetraceEntry
rules.quote: First signal bar makes highest high of last X (5-10) bars with no higher bar since. Second signal bars occurs within next X bars and makes the lowest low in last X bars and is lowest bar since. Enter short on retracement to top Y (~50)% of second signal bar.
rules.description: Short as written; pseudocode is the long mirror: bar a made the lowest low of X bars with no lower low since; bar b, 1..X bars after a, made the highest high of X bars with no higher high since; enter long on the first close inside the bottom Y of bar b's range.
rules.book_order_type: limit into the top Y of bar 2; mechanized as a close inside the zone, next open (TRIAGE)

complexity.reason: two anchored window extremes and an armed zone

library_check.evidence: FibonacciRetracementLevel retraces a fixed window's span; this retraces into the second signal bar's own range after a high-then-low sequence. Nothing matches the two-signal-bar structure.

notes: maxWaitBars bounds how old bar b may be (not in the note).
'Within the next X bars' read as 1..X bars after bar a.

rules.name: DonchianOutsizedBreakoutFade
rules.quote: Donchian channel with look back length of 20. One (large) bar with a low below the midline and a high that shifts the top channel up. Enter short
rules.description: Against the 20-bar Donchian channel of the bars ending one bar ago: the bar's high exceeds the channel top while its low is below the channel midline: short (fade). Long mirrors (low below the bottom, high above the midline).

library_check.evidence: AtrBandBreakout and the Donchian breakout family (HighestHighBreakout, CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh) trade WITH the channel break; OutsideBarInMidRange tests an outside bar's midpoint in the range. None fades a bar that spans from below the midline through the top.

notes: 'Large' is implied by spanning half the channel; minRangeAtr (default 0, off) makes it explicit.

rules.name: BreakoutClearsByHalfBar
rules.quote: X bar breakout high where the high of the last X bars is below the midpoint of the breakout bar
rules.description: The prior X-bar high is below the current bar's midpoint, so the bar breaks out by at least half its own range. Long; short mirrors (prior X-bar low above the midpoint).

library_check.evidence: BreakoutClearsPriorExtremeByMargin clears Highest(High, N)[1] by a fixed tick margin; here the margin is half the breakout bar's own range, so the two fire on different bars at any fixed margin. CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh (EEC) is the close-through form.

notes: midpoint > prior high implies high > prior high, so no separate breakout test is needed.

primitives_to_inline.name: LargeShapedBarAtLag
primitives_to_inline.quote: A large bullish bar (> 2 ATR but less than 7 just to avoid weird case with huge bar ; Open in bottom quarter ; close in top quarter)
primitives_to_inline.description: The bar `lag` bars ago is a large bull bar of a given shape: range between minRangeAtr and maxRangeAtr x ATR (ATR as of that bar), open in the bottom openFraction of its range, close in the top closeFraction. Short side: a bear bar, open in the top, close in the bottom. Shared by ON-12-b and ON-13, and at other defaults by ON-21 (standard bar) and ON-24 (huge bar).

complexity.reason: Single-bar arithmetic against an ATR read from a series variable.

library_check.evidence: At lag 0 and maxRangeAtr large this is OpenNearBarLow(0.25) AND CloseRangePosition(0.75) AND BarRangeAtrMultiple(2, N) - three existing rules ANDed. The cap, and reading all three at a lag against the ATR as of that bar, are what the pattern rules need and the existing rules lack. ClimaxBar (Brooks) tests a body fraction instead of open/close positions.

notes: ATR length is not given in #12/#13 (the note lists per-timeframe ATR lookbacks for the stops); 20 assumed.
Strict > / < for the size band per the note ('> 2 ATR but less than 7').
CloseRangePosition, one of the three rules this decomposes into at lag 0, is a Davey (EEC) rule: provenance to surface if the authoring pass reuses it.

resolutions.answer: HIGH candle = CLOSE above the 50-bar high (symmetric with LOW). Every bar between the two L's (H's) must be a C candle.
Level = a cluster of wick lows within a tolerance, built like the I2 support zone (not the most recent swing low).

Zone: scanning back N bars, the K+ most recent 1-bar swing lows all within X*ATR of each other, with std dev of those lows <= k*ATR; bottom = lowest of them; a close more than 0.5*ATR below the bottom kills it. #26 needs two distinct stacked zones. No pane-2 'near zone' condition for now.
A bar that is both a swing high and a swing low counts as both, ordered by bar direction: a green bar (close > open) is low-then-high, a red bar high-then-low.
The mirror order (high, low, high, low with the last two inside the first two) also counts.
Breakaway move = a run of consecutive bull bars each with range >= k*ATR; measured from the first run bar's open to the run's highest high.
Cancel the armed setup if a later bar trades back into the band. Add a window input W, counted from the wick bar, constrained W > Z.
'Fractal low length ~3' = swing strength 3 (three bars each side); the pullback must be at least 3 bars.
